cohort: 1,115 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies and a BMI >30, out of a total of 9,954 pregnant women
finding: Women with high BMI enrolled in a specialised antenatal management programme received increased care and had superior breastfeeding initiation rates, but engagement was poor and there were no significant differences in antenatal or postnatal complications, mode of birth, or neonatal outcome.
mod_finding: No significant difference was noted in Caesarean rate (30% vs 32%).
birth_weight: Intervention group: 3538 g, Control group: 3560 g
